title: Named-root clear returns 502 when the control reply misses its budget, and the identical retry then gets 409 because the pending producer intent belongs to the original call
outcome: A termal_name_source_root clear whose control reply arrives after its budget can be settled by the documented identical retry: the retry returns the original outcome instead of a 409 conflict. Or the 502 states a different, working settlement route. A pending producer intent never stays unsettled indefinitely after the caller's claim ends.
acceptance: A note identifies, from source, why an identical retry of a named-root clear whose first attempt returned 502 ('named-root control reply arrived after its budget; retry the same request to settle any pending intent') is refused with 409 ('pending producer intent belongs to its existing owner; entry retained'): what identifies the intent's owner, and why the retry is not recognized as the same owner and request.

The identical retry settles the pending intent and returns its final outcome, or the 502's guidance is corrected to a working route. A pending intent left after its claim is released or completed is settled or retired by a documented rule, with no live claim touched.

Focused tests reproduce a late control reply for a clear request followed by an identical retry; the full gate passes and an independent review pair has no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
